content:
elsa (support): heads-up — Osprey Labs just opened a ticket: dedicated cluster 02 is rejecting requests intermittently with 429 AdmissionControl and a burst TPS violation. Customer reports elevated latency and auth failures mixed in.

raj (osprey-cust): yes, started ~10:12 UTC. some calls return 401, a bunch 429. dashboard shows sudden TPS spike ~3x baseline. no config changes on our side.

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-20260317-4335 — AdmissionControl throttling on dedicated-cluster-02. Assigned to @matt (sre).

matt (sre): looking. can you paste example request ids or short curl to repro? also will pull admission metrics and GPU util.

raj (osprey-cust): sample req id: req_8f3a2c. curl: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -d '{"model":"rwd-7b","input":"ping"}' -v` — returns 429 with body `{\"error\":\"AdmissionControl: burst credits depleted\"}`

anya (eng-runtime): thanks. initial glance at telemetry: cluster-02 spike aligns with a noisy-tenant (tenant id t-992) that started sending long context chat loops. GPU mem and SM utilization hit 94% for ~8m. Admission controller started shedding to maintain token-per-second SLO.

zoe (eng-platform): autoscaler logs show a failed scale-up window at 10:13 UTC — scale decision returned `no-compatible-node` due to instance group quota. So we couldn't add nodes despite demand.

matt (sre): that explains admission fallback. two parallel issues: noisy neighbor saturating capacity + autoscaler blocked by infra quota. short term mitigation ideas: 1) apply per-tenant soft throttle (limit t-992), 2) add burst credits to Osprey while infra quota is addressed, 3) promote requests to a compatible model variant with lower token cost.

elsa (support): raj — can we temporarily isolate Osprey to a fallback pool? we can enable dedicated admission headroom bump and grant 10k burst tokens for 30m while platform resolves scale.

raj (osprey-cust): fallback pool? would that break routing? we need minimal disruption — some requests are latency sensitive.

anya (eng-runtime): fallback is non-disruptive: we route to a smaller-capacity fleet with strict batching. perf will be slightly worse but stable. we can also auto-inject `x-priority: high` header for latency-sensitive routes to bypass some batching delays.

matt (sre): I'm going to: 1) apply tenant throttle to t-992 -> cap at 0.5x current TPS; 2) raise Osprey burst credits by 30% (temporary); 3) trigger manual node spin-up request to infra. Doing the throttle now.

oncall-bot: Action logged: throttle applied to tenant t-992 by matt at 10:22 UTC.

matt (sre): throttle is active. seeing drop in aggregate token generation. admission 429s for Osprey drop by ~60% in the last 2m.

elsa (support): raj — we added temporary burst credits and applied throttle on the noisy tenant. please verify if your 401s persist.

raj (osprey-cust): 401s appear to have stopped. latency still elevated for some user flows (~800ms vs 200ms baseline) but stable. thanks.

anya (eng-runtime): note from runtime: KV cache eviction spiked during the saturation window causing cold-cache token cost — that contributes to higher latency. We'll roll a small patch to reduce aggressive cache eviction (config flag `cache.eviction_aggressiveness`) and revert if it causes mem pressure.

zoe (eng-platform): infra request for extra quota submitted (ticket INF-8812). ETA 45m for approval. Will monitor.

matt (sre): follow-up operational checklist for support thread:
- collect `admission_controller.metrics` and `gpu.utilization` around window (done)
- export a small repro script for eng-runtime (attached below)
- capture per-tenant token/sec and burst-credit usage (done)
- confirm autoscaler config: scale_up cooldown 120s, max_unavailable 1, node_family preference G5.

anya (eng-runtime): repro script (use to simulate noisy tenant):
```
# simulate sustained long contexts
for i in {1..500}; do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $NOISY_KEY" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"rwd-7b","input":"repeat long context... (2000 tokens)"}' &
done
wait
```

matt (sre): log excerpt showing admission decisions:```
[10:11:32] AdmissionController: enqueue req req_8f3a2c tokens=512
[10:11:33] AdmissionController: admit req req_8f3a2c -> REJECT (burst credits depleted)
[10:11:33] Router: 401 returned for req req_8f3a2c due to auth handshake timeout
[10:12:05] NodeManager: scale attempt -> rejected (quota limit)
[10:13:40] AdmissionController: throttle applied to tenant t-992 -> OK
```

elsa (support): customer asked for post-mortem steps and a short-run playbook to avoid recurrence. proposing:
- enforce per-tenant rate-limits by default on Dedicated (soft limits with escalation)
- add a guard in autoscaler to surface infra quota blocks earlier to ops and support
- increase default headroom for Dedicated clusters by 20% until autoscaler quotas are stable
- add an automated failover to a 'reduced-capacity fallback pool' for latency-sensitive customers

zoe (eng-platform): agree. small note — increasing headroom will raise cost for Dedicated customers; product should ok before we change default. propose a targeted setting for customers flagged as latency-sensitive.

anya (eng-runtime): I'll open PR for `cache.eviction_aggressiveness` default from 0.7 -> 0.5 and add a feature flag `runtime.reduced_eviction` for quick rollback. Also add metric `admission.queueing_time_p95` to the console.

matt (sre): closing the immediate incident. actions: we leave throttle on for noisy tenant until quota resolved, burst credits remain for 30m, infra ticket in progress. I'll prepare incident note for postmortem.

raj (osprey-cust): appreciate the quick response. request a short timeline and postmortem when available.

elsa (support): will follow up with PM and send timeline. tagging @zach-prod for heads up on cost impact. :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: INC-20260317-4335 status -> mitigated.

matt (sre): final note — for on-call runbook: if admission 429s spike and autoscaler is blocked by quota, do: 1) identify noisy tenant via per-tenant TPS, 2) apply transient throttle, 3) grant temporary burst credits to affected customer, 4) open infra quota request, 5) prepare fallback routing. will add to runbook doc.

elsa (support): thread summary will be posted to customer and appended to ticket.

raj (osprey-cust): thanks everyone.
